sections.history: Tirusaathamangai, now the village of Seeyathamangai, lies about 13 km from Nagapattinam on the Nagapattinam–Nagore–Kumbakonam road, near the Nagapattinam–Tiruvarur boundary (one listing gives Nannilam taluk, Tiruvarur district). It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The temple is locally known as Ayavanthi, and the stone shrine is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Ayavandeeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Malarkkannammai — also Irumalarkannammai, and in Sanskrit Ubaya-Pushpa-Vilochani, 'she of the two flower-eyes' — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The temple keeps the simple, well-ordered plan of the smaller Kaveri-country sanctuaries.
sections.legends: The goddess's names all turn on the beauty of her eyes: Malarkkannammai and Irumalarkannammai in Tamil, Ubaya-Pushpa-Vilochani in Sanskrit, each meaning 'she whose two eyes are like flowers.' This tender image is the devotional heart of the shrine. As with many smaller delta temples, the fuller sthala purana is preserved chiefly in the local tradition and in Sambandar's Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail between Nagapattinam and Kumbakonam include Seeyathamangai among their stops.
sections.experience: At Seeyathamangai the pilgrim comes to a gentle delta shrine, the Ayavanthi, loved above all for its flower-eyed goddess. Before Ayavandeeswarar and Malarkkannammai, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a small Tevaram temple on the quiet road from Nagapattinam to the Kaveri country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Seeyathamangai is about 13 km from Nagapattinam on the Nagapattinam–Nagore–Kumbakonam road, near the Nagapattinam–Tiruvarur boundary (one listing gives Nannilam taluk). Nagapattinam is the nearest major rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
